textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · Living Creatures: Exploring their Characteristics · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Living things share certain characteristics. They need food, they breathe, they grow, they respond to changes, they reproduce and they die.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Living things share certain characteristics. They need food, they breathe, they grow, they respond to changes, they reproduce and they die. A stone or a toy does not show these characteristics, so it is non-living.
beats.speakEn: Living things share certain characteristics. They need food, they breathe, they grow, they respond to changes, they reproduce and they die. A stone or a toy does not show these characteristics, so it is non-living.

beats.en: Living things need water, a source of energy and surroundings that meet their needs. Plants and animals also exchange gases with their surroundings. Plants make their own food using sunlight.
beats.speakEn: Living things need water, a source of energy and surroundings that meet their needs. Plants and animals also exchange gases with their surroundings. Plants make their own food using sunlight.

textbookBox.concept: A seed needs water, air and a suitable temperature to germinate, which means to sprout. In a typical bean seedling, the root grows downward and the shoot grows upward.

beats.en: A seed needs water, air and a suitable temperature to germinate, which means to sprout. In a typical bean seedling, the root grows downward and the shoot grows upward.
beats.speakEn: A seed needs water, air and a suitable temperature to germinate, which means to sprout. In a typical bean seedling, the root grows downward and the shoot grows upward.

beats.en: A flowering plant can grow from seed to seedling to adult plant. A flower may become a fruit containing new seeds, and the cycle can begin again. Many animals change form as they grow.
beats.speakEn: A flowering plant can grow from seed to seedling to adult plant. A flower may become a fruit containing new seeds, and the cycle can begin again. Many animals change form as they grow.
